sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

sheets.name: ITERATIONS
rows: Remove the unconditional sh:minCount/qualifiedMinCount requirements that force every ship to have a hull-area assignment; the conditional rule for existing other ice-strengthened areas does not independently require such an area to exist. Use SHACL Core conditional logic so the parameter and fixed AR = 3.6 constraints apply when an existing assignment identifies the relevant area, while retaining the declared ship ownership of the quantity properties. The COMPLETE contract also requires the controlled value nltl:otherIceStrengthenedAreaValue, but the candidate omits it and no compatible canonical relationship/path to that value was supplied; locate that canonical path through the matcher rather than substituting nltl:otherIceStrengthenedArea, relocating the value, or using the unconstrained mandatory nltl:hullArea string as a proxy. Preserve the exact inclusive AR bounds, units, and the strict angle boundaries.

REVERSAL: Newly supplied canonical range metadata and the COMPLETE contract now show that both controlled values are required: nltl:assignedHullArea has range nltl:hullAreaValue, so it must identify the assignment with nltl:otherIceStrengthenedArea, not the range-incompatible nltl:otherIceStrengthenedAreaValue; the latter is separately a nltl:hullRegionValue. Replace the assignment shape’s current hasValue accordingly, and locate through the matcher the canonical owner-compatible relationship/path needed to represent nltl:otherIceStrengthenedAreaValue rather than relocating it or using nltl:hullArea as a proxy. Also repair the bow applicability alternatives: every non-applicable angle branch must require nltl:bowFormApplicability false, while the conjunction gamma > 0 degrees, gamma < 80 degrees, and beta' > 10 degrees must require true. The current non-applicable branches ignore the boolean and therefore allow a true applicability value with disqualifying angles. Preserve optional existence of the area assignment, conditional parameter checks on an existing matching assignment, ship ownership of the quantities, exact inclusive AR = 3.6, units, and strict angle boundaries.
